messages.subject: Linear combinations
parts:
Hi,

I have been trying to compute some linear combinations and I have encountered some problems...


- Is it possible to compute linear combinations of the linear predictors in the
scale of the response for non-Gaussian models. For example, a linear combination
of the predicted probabilities in a Binomial model.

- R-INLA seems to complain when the linear combination is made of a single term, e.g., 
a number by a covariate coefficient. I know that this is easy to compute but I'd prefer INLA
to do it to avoid using any extra code. Is there any simple workaround?

- Function inla.make.lincombs() does not seem to find the object that I pass (called 'lc') from within
a function. It seems to work when 'lcl' is defined in the global workspace. Looking at the code, i see that 
inla.make.lincombs() does not take a named argument but that looks for the object in a "funny" way... :)

Many thanks,

Virgilio
